candidates.summary: the sweep converted three write rules to the declaring-node test and left the fourth member, the cur-call provenance switch, so a crossing function's realm-typed named result is accepted as a frame identity at preprocess and only the runtime backstop refuses it, naming the wrong cause
candidates.failure_scenario: func Target(cur realm){}; func F(_ realm) (cur realm) { Target(cur); return }. `_ realm` is legal as a crossing first parameter (preprocess.go:2827 admits the `.arg` form), so `cur` here is a named RESULT whose declaring block node is a crossing FuncDecl. The provenance switch's two `if !dft.IsCrossing()` arms (L2160, L2169) test only that declaring node, exactly like the new isCrossingCurParam, so preprocess accepts the forward. The realm then panics at call time with "crossing function gno.land/r/demo/curprov.Target was entered without cross() ... a stale capture from another frame, a sibling frame, or a rebound cur", which describes a different mistake than the one written: the developer passed a named result, not a stale capture. The same shape with a non-crossing declarer is refused at preprocess with the right message, so a realm deploys and fails on call instead of failing to compile. Fail-closed (the identity backstop holds) and pre-existing: the provenance switch is unchanged by the diff. In scope because this diff sweeps that class, rewriting three of its members into isCrossingCurParam, and the PR body states the write rule now makes "the same test the cur-call provenance check makes, so 'may be cur-called' and 'may not be written' agree by construction" — at the reviewed sha they agree on a test that is wrong in both directions, refusing the write of that named result while accepting its forward.

candidates.summary: crossingFromTestFile is the package's existing "this call came from test code" test and the new harness carve-out does not use it, so the VM now carries three disagreeing spellings of the same predicate
candidates.failure_scenario: op_call.go:229 exempts a crossing entry when the caller's file name ends `_test.gno`; preprocess.go:2070 exempts a whole package when the node being preprocessed has PkgPath `testing`; the diff adds a third at op_call.go:560 keyed on the immediate caller frame's PkgPath being `testing`. The three disagree on the cells that matter: a `_test.gno` caller that seeds a cur without routing through package testing is exempt from the realm-package gate and not from the identity gate, and a helper in package testing dispatching from a non-test file is exempt from the identity gate. A future harness path lands in whichever cell nobody wrote a fixture for, and the fix is then a fourth spelling.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'TestingBasePkgPath\|crossingFromTestFile' gnovm/pkg/gnolang/*.go and read each site's predicate
candidates.evidence: op_call.go:229 crossingFromTestFile → strings.HasSuffix(fv.FileName, "_test.gno"); preprocess.go:2070 ctxpn.PkgPath == TestingBasePkgPath; op_call.go:560 caller.Func.PkgPath == TestingBasePkgPath.

dropped.summary: the AssignStmt write rule lost its `n.Op != DEFINE` guard while the RangeStmt sibling kept it, so a declaration is now judged as a rebind
dropped.settled_by: The asymmetry is correct and deliberate. gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_cur_reassign_define.gno pins the DEFINE case with `// Error: ... cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter` and its header states the reason: a `:=` whose name is already declared in the same block assigns that slot. A RangeStmt pushes its own block at TRANS_BLOCK (pushInitBlock) and defines the key and value there, so a range DEFINE always declares a new binding and the guard it keeps is the right one. Every remaining DEFINE spelling (if-init, switch-init, for-init, inner BlockStmt) also lands in a pushed block, pinned by zrealm_cur_shadow.gno and zrealm_cur_shadow_if.gno.
